page.title: Marbella Boat Rental in February: What to Expect

data.meta_description: Planning a marbella boat rental weather february trip? See sea temps, wind odds, sunny days, and which boats sail from Puerto Banús this winter.
data.summary: February in Marbella offers 16°C air, 15°C sea, and calm mornings ideal for a 2-hour charter. Our guide covers what to expect, what to wear, and which boats run from Puerto Banús.
key_facts: Wind: 8-12 kts; mornings calmer than afternoons
All charters include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, IVA
February is low season – more availability, lower prices

faq.q: Is it warm enough for a boat trip in February in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, for a short cruise. Air temperatures average 16°C, often reaching 19°C in the afternoon sun. Sea temperature is 15°C, so swimming is brisk but possible if you're hardy. Most February charters are sightseeing trips rather than swim stops – you'll be comfortable in a light jacket or jumper, and the boat's cabin provides shelter.

faq.q: What is the weather like in February in Marbella?
faq.a: February is mild and partly cloudy. You'll get around 6 hours of sunshine daily, with rain on roughly 5-6 days in the month. Winds are typically 8-12 knots, with mornings calmer than afternoons. Sea state is generally slight to moderate – suitable for our 12m+ flybridge and motor yachts, which handle the chop well.

faq.q: Which boats are available for charter in February?
faq.a: All our fleet operates year-round from Puerto Banús. For a 2-hour winter cruise, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both 12.5m) are ideal – they're enclosed, heated, and cost €749/2h. For a longer day, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is available from €4,719 for 4 hours, including a free jet ski. Other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 are available on request.

faq.q: What should I wear for a February boat trip in Marbella?
faq.a: Layers are key. Start with a thermal base, add a fleece or jumper, and top with a windproof jacket. Bring a hat and sunglasses – the sun is still strong. Non-slip shoes are essential. The boat provides blankets and a heated cabin, but you'll want to be outside for the views. Don't forget sunscreen – UV is still moderate.

faq.q: Can we swim or use the jet ski in February?
faq.a: Swimming is possible but cold – sea temp is 15°C. Most February guests skip the swim and enjoy the cruise instead. The jet ski included with the Mangusta 80 can be used, but you'll need a wetsuit (we can arrange one on request). If you're keen on water sports, consider a March or April charter when the sea warms to 17-18°C.

faq.q: Is February a good time to book a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, for several reasons. You'll have more availability, especially for weekends. Prices are at their lowest – Tier A boats are €749/2h versus €1,200+ in peak summer. You'll also enjoy quieter waters and unobstructed views of La Concha and the Marbella coastline. Just be flexible with the forecast – we can reschedule if a storm front passes.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my charter?
faq.a: Our skippers monitor conditions closely. If sea conditions are unsafe (winds above 25 knots or heavy rain), we'll offer a full refund or reschedule to the next available day. In February, we typically see 2-3 weather-affected days per month. For marginal conditions, we'll recommend a shorter charter (2h) and stay within the sheltered bay.

faq.q: Do you provide food and drinks on February charters?
faq.a: Yes, all charters include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks – regardless of season. For February, we can also prepare a hot drink (coffee or tea) on request. If you'd like a full meal, you can order a catering package (e.g., seafood paella) at least 48 hours in advance – prices on request via WhatsApp.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a marbella boat rental weather february trip? You're in for a treat: February in Marbella is mild, calm, and gloriously uncrowded. Average air temperatures sit at 16°C (often hitting 19°C in the afternoon), sea temperatures at 15°C, and you'll enjoy around 6 hours of daily sunshine. While it's not swimsuit weather for most, it's perfect for a scenic cruise along the Costa del Sol, with the snow-capped peaks of La Concha as a backdrop. Here's exactly what to expect – and how to make the most of a winter charter from Puerto Banús.

February Weather Snapshot for Marbella

February is one of Marbella's cooler, wetter months, but 'wet' is relative – you'll see rain on about 5-6 days, usually as short showers. The rest of the time, expect partly cloudy skies with sunny spells. Winds average 8-12 knots, with mornings significantly calmer than afternoons. Sea state is typically slight to moderate (1-2 on the Beaufort scale), which is easily handled by our fleet.

MetricFebruary Average
Air temperature16°C (high 19°C)
Sea temperature15°C
Sunshine6 hours/day
Rain days5-6 days
Wind speed8-12 kts
Sea stateSlight to moderate

For the most stable conditions, book a morning departure (10:00 or 12:00) – the sea is glassier and the light is beautiful for photography.

What to Expect on Board in February

Our boats are fully equipped for winter cruising. All have heated interiors (flybridge models have enclosed saloons), plus blankets and windbreaks on deck. You'll still want to spend time outside – the views of the Sierra Blanca and the Marbella coastline are stunning. A 2-hour charter is ideal: you'll cruise past the Golden Mile, see the luxury villas of Río Verde, and get a close-up of Puerto Banús from the water.

If you're feeling adventurous, you can take a dip – but 15°C water is invigorating, to say the least. Most February guests prefer to stay dry and enjoy the complimentary drinks and snacks on board.

Which Boats Are Best for February?

For a marbella boat rental weather february trip, we recommend the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 – both 12.5m, with enclosed saloons and flybridges. They're perfect for 2-hour winter cruises and cost €749 for 2 hours (all inclusive). If you want more space and a free jet ski, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is available from €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours – the jet ski adds a splash of excitement if you're brave enough to ride in February.

For larger groups (up to 12 guests), the Ferretti 94 (29m) or Canados 86 (26m) are excellent choices – pricing on request via WhatsApp. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.

What's Included in Every Charter

No hidden extras – every booking includes:

  • Licensed skipper
  • Fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (nuts, olives, crisps)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You can also request a hot drink (coffee/tea) on board – free of charge in February.

Best Routes for a February Cruise

With calm seas, you have several options:

  • Puerto Banús to Cabopino (east): 45 minutes each way – spot the dunes and the marina, then return.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona (west): 1 hour each way – see the old town from the sea.
  • Golden Mile sightseeing: stay close to shore for the best villa views.

If the wind picks up, your skipper will adjust the route to stay in sheltered waters – safety first, always.

Why February Is a Smart Choice

You'll have the coast almost to yourself. No summer crowds, no queue at the marina, and often better prices. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749/2h – in July, the same charter costs €1,200+. You'll also enjoy a more personal experience, as skippers have more time to share local stories and point out landmarks like La Concha and the Sierra Blanca.

Just be flexible: if a storm front moves in, we'll happily reschedule – no penalty.

How to Book Your February Charter

Booking is simple. Choose your boat from our fleet overview, then contact us via WhatsApp for availability. For boats other than the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, or Mangusta 80, we'll provide a custom quote within hours. We recommend booking at least 3-4 days in advance for weekend slots, but last-minute bookings are often possible on weekdays.

For more seasonal guidance, see our January guide or March guide. And if you're planning ahead, our April guide covers the start of swim season.
